issues.description: The problem statement UML and text require a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal): int, but the template and solution use different names inconsistently: the template's Main calls computeMealCost(...), the solution's SealSaloon implements computeMealCost(Meal) as the static price-calculation method, while the solution's Main (commented code) still calls calculateTotalPrice(...). This name/signature inconsistency across artifacts will confuse students about which method to implement and which name to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across problem statement, template, and solution. Either (A) rename the static method in SealSaloon from computeMealCost to calculateTotalPrice and update all Main usages to call calculateTotalPrice(Meal), or (B) update the problem statement and UML to require computeMealCost(Meal): int and update any Main examples to call computeMealCost. Ensure the template, tests, and solution all use the same method name and signature.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal) for computing a meal's net cost, but the implementation in SealSaloon defines a static method named computeMealCost(Meal). Additionally, example usage across repositories is inconsistent: the template Main expects computeMealCost, while the solution Main calls calculateTotalPrice. This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual operation (computing the total price of a Meal) creates confusion for students mapping requirements to implementation and may cause compile/runtime errors due to mismatched method names.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent name for the meal-cost method across all artifacts. Rename computeMealCost to calculateTotalPrice in SealSaloon (and update any callers), or alternatively update the problem statement and Main usages to use computeMealCost everywhere. Prefer matching the problem statement's calculateTotalPrice to avoid student confusion.
